LungLogic: Model-Based Airflow Control
with Measured-Delay Compensation and Auto PID
ME-12-TYIN-007 | Yuqiao Li, Chun Yin Ku (John), Jiaquan Zhong | Supervisors: Jonathan Eden, Ying Tan | Mechatronics Engineering
1. Introduction
1.1 Project need
Dynamic lung phantoms support imaging and ventilation research. Existing products and laboratory systems do not combine programmable timing, repeatable volume and independent left/right actuation.
1.2 Project objective
LungLogic develops a pneumatic and software platform to control a medical biomimetic lung model. This stage validates one 250 mL branch before bilateral integration.
1.3 Nominal breathing reference
Breathing-cycle illustration at 15 bpm and I:E = 1:2.
RR · respiratory rate12–16 bpm; nominal 15 bpm
I:E · inhale:exhale time1:2; 1.33 s / 2.67 s at 15 bpm
VT · tidal volume250 mL per branch
RepeatabilityVT error within ±5%
Nominal design values, not measured performance. The 250 mL branch target is half of the ~500 mL adult tidal-volume example.
Source: 4DMedical project scope, 19 March 2026, pp. 5 and 13. The ±5% repeatability value is a design target.

The controller runs the 100 Hz breathing and flow loop. The bridge connects logic to the routing valves, PPV and SFM3300 sensor.
Fig. 2. Control architecture and bridge PCB.
3. Integrated Control System & Software
3.1 Objective
Track flow and tidal volume with a visible, repeatable closed-loop system. Feedforward supplies the nominal valve command; sensor feedback corrects error.

3.4 Auto PID and measured-delay compensation
Auto PID scores bounded Kp/Ki trials. Smith prediction uses the identified model and measured delay; hardware adds no artificial delay.
